chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

When you buy your sacrificial animal, and weigh its price, and it becomes in your saddle (or among your riding animals), then the offering has reached its place. So if you wish to shave (your head), then shave.
ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to shave the head during Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the precise moment the sacrificial animal (Hady) is considered consecrated, linking the completion of its purchase and placement to the pilgrim's option to shave their head and exit Ihram. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the ritual status of the animal as the trigger for the permissibility of grooming, distinguishing between the act of sacrifice and the subsequent rites. This ruling underscores the flexibility within the Hajj rituals, allowing pilgrims to choose shaving over shortening once the Hady is fully designated.
